report.summary: Reviewed the supplied packet only: assessment-label-citations.ts, delivery-assessment.ts, assessment-label-source-facts.test.ts and the project skill. No files or commands were run. The foreign-subtree-text fix is in the right place and fails closed. The traversal at lines 68-75 has no cycle guard, so a hostile recursive SVG document reaches the 50,000-visit cap. That cap makes every label witness unresolved, both the positive one and the absence witness. This matches the task requirement, but it turns the walk into a denial-of-service amplifier. I found no defect in the negative gate, the canonical explanation or the linked-business skip, and no change to strict output. The packet does not include exact-copy-directive.ts, so I could not check what the normalizer (normalized) strips.
limitations: Packet scope only. Files that are imported but not supplied were not inspected, including exact-copy-directive.ts (the normalizer normalized), source-literal-directive.ts (how html_labels and its context are parsed), static-resources.ts (staticFileKind), assessment-limits.ts and contracts.ts.

Things that could not be checked: what normalized() treats as whitespace and whether it strips zero-width characters, how the html_labels directive's context and labels are parsed, and which staticFileKind values the .HTML case-insensitivity test relies on.

Nothing was executed. All findings about the cycles and text counting come from reading parse5's default tree adapter semantics (entity-decoded #text value, parent pointer present) and from reading the code. They are labelled as unexecuted reasoning, not observed behaviour.
The exported function labelsIn (line 18) is only called from within this module in the packet. Whether other modules outside the packet call it was not checked.

The no-findings result rests on inference for: PAGE requiring only declared HTML label text (lines 55-83 and 144-146 ignore any for/id association); FORM requiring a common owner, with unresolved owners disabling the absence fact (lines 88-99 and 136); the strict output path (delivery-assessment.ts lines 248-263, keys/record/text checks unchanged); the linked-business skip (lines 308-309 and 470-471); and the canonical explanation (lines 151-162). All were read, but none was proven by a run.
The source-with-line-numbers text is treated as the complete file. Hashing and byte counts were not verified, and the line numbers cited assume the given line map matches the real file.

An SVG <title> inside a label counts as foreign text, so it makes the label witness unknown. This is a conservative false unknown, not a defect, and the packet says no future sealed corpus is supplied.
Item-level delivery-assessment semantics outside label handling were not re-audited, because the task scope is the label fix, the negative gate, the explanation, the business skip and strict outputs.
